messages.text: I am cataloging the Lantern Marsh greenhouse trays before the spring volunteers arrive.
Are the clay labels part of the inventory?
Yes, but the east bench has three cracked saucers, so I am moving those first.
The old inventory sheet says row labels were sorted by plant name last year.
That could explain why volunteers missed the bay numbers.
For this season, I prefer pot labels grouped by bench row; people find trays faster that way.
I printed the sheet, but Neri spotted the old sort when we checked the north bench.
Should the sheet be reissued?
Not today. I will ask Ivo to check the west shelf before changing the paper.
I checked that west shelf. The cracked saucers are on the bottom rack.
Does the sorting preference still apply to the labels?
Yes, row first is still easier. The amber seedlings need their own tray because they dry quickly.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: pot labels grouped by bench row for this season

evidence.quote: For this season, I prefer pot labels grouped by bench row
Yes, row first is still easier.

messages.text: The Blue Hour observatory is making a paper atlas for the winter visitors.
Do you already have a place for the moon chart?
The west table is open, though the tripod case still blocks one corner.
Dr. Venn is checking whether the balcony map can be printed at the larger scale.
Would that change where the chart goes?
If Dr. Venn signs off by Friday, I plan to reserve the west table for the moon chart.
The scale review is late, so I have not sent the reservation request.
Could you use the north stand instead?
Maybe, but it faces the service door and visitors crowd there after the talk.
The review came back yesterday, but it asks for one more projection check.
Then the west table is still unreserved.
Right. I am leaving the floor plan in pencil until the check is done.
The projection check passed this morning. I still need to ask the caretaker about the table, so the reservation is not complete.
That makes sense. The west table remains open until the caretaker confirms the aisle width.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: reserve the west table for the moon chart if Dr. Venn signs off by Friday

evidence.quote: If Dr. Venn signs off by Friday, I plan to reserve the west table for the moon chart

messages.text: The Tideline archive needs a rota for the evening chart readers.
I can draft a rota that alternates the two reading rooms.
Please draft it, but keep the west room free for the map cases.
I will send the alternating-room draft to the coordinator after you review it.
That is your draft plan. I have not approved a schedule or sent anything.
Understood. I will leave the file marked draft.
The coordinator found an old key list mixed into the rota folder.
I can remove it from the working copy.
Keep the old list in the archive. It explains why the west room key was missing.
The coordinator asked whether the alternating-room schedule is final.
It is not. I only asked you to prepare a draft for discussion.
I will mark it as awaiting review.

expected.subject: the assistant
expected.object: send the alternating-room draft to the coordinator after user review

evidence.quote: I will send the alternating-room draft to the coordinator after you review it
I have not approved a schedule or sent anything.
It is not. I only asked you to prepare a draft for discussion.

messages.text: The Ashgrove makerspace is revising its kiln checklist before the tile workshop.
Is the card written for the old kiln model?
I think so. The newer controller has a separate cooling indicator.
The card says, "Switch off the kiln before loading a test tile." That is the card speaking, not a request from me.
I will treat that as quoted checklist text.
The margin note says the rule was added after a cracked shelf, but it does not name the kiln model.
Miro brought the updated controller guide, and its pictures show a different latch.
Should the old card be removed?
Not until the workshop lead compares both versions.
We found the card belongs in the retired-equipment folder.
Does that confirm the instruction applies to the new kiln?
No, the folder only tells us which card is old. The lead still has to check the new model.

expected.subject: the Ashgrove checklist card
expected.object: switch off the kiln before loading a test tile

evidence.quote: Switch off the kiln before loading a test tile

messages.text: The archive annex is being cleared before the map boxes are moved.
Is the portable heater still stored there?
I do not use the portable heater in the annex; its cord is frayed.
The facilities crew tagged the heater for inspection.
Did they find a replacement cord?
They have not checked it yet. I moved the paper maps away from the outlet.
The annex has a draft near the loading door, so the boxes need a cover.
Could the crew bring a safe heater?
They can decide that after inspection; I am not choosing equipment for that room.
The heater is still tagged. The crew asked us to keep the aisle open.
That leaves room for the map cart.
Yes, and the paper boxes are now on the raised shelf.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: portable heater in the archive annex

evidence.quote: I do not use the portable heater in the annex

messages.text: The Red Kiln ceramic fair is changing its visitor route for the courtyard repairs.
Which door is open during the repair week?
From 2026-05-12 through 2026-05-18, I used the east entrance while the courtyard was closed.
The printed volunteer note says the east door stays open after the repair week.
Was that copied from last year?
Probably. I have not checked the latest schedule yet.
Correction: the courtyard reopened on 2026-05-19, and I have used the courtyard door since then.
So the east entrance was temporary.
Yes. The east door is now for deliveries, not the visitor route.
The fair guide still lists the east entrance on its first page.
Should it be updated before the weekend?
I asked the guide team to change it. I do not know when they will publish the revision.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: the east entrance at the Red Kiln ceramic fair

evidence.quote: From 2026-05-12 through 2026-05-18, I used the east entrance

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: the courtyard door at the Red Kiln ceramic fair

evidence.quote: Correction: the courtyard reopened on 2026-05-19, and I have used the courtyard door since then.

messages.text: The Juniper astronomy club is sorting keys for the rooftop observation nights.
Who keeps the balcony key?
Elise Mora keeps the balcony key. Elise Tan lent us the narrow-field filter.
The old checkout note just says Elise, which is why the filter return went to the wrong shelf.
Would adding surnames fix that?
Yes, the two Elis are different members and should not share one key record.
Elise left a note saying she will bring the filter to Friday practice.
Do you know which Elise wrote that?
No. The note has no surname, so I cannot tell whether it is Mora or Tan.
Mora confirmed the key is in the rooftop lockbox.
And the filter?
Tan returned it to the optics drawer. I updated those as separate entries.

expected.subject: Mora
expected.object: the balcony key she keeps is in the rooftop lockbox

evidence.quote: Elise Mora keeps the balcony key.
Mora confirmed the key is in the rooftop lockbox.

messages.text: The North Quay tool shed is changing its volunteer hours for the summer.
Has the caretaker posted the schedule?
Not on the gate yet. There is a handwritten note in the office.
Mara thinks the north shed may close before dusk, but she has not heard it from the caretaker.
So that is a report to check, not a confirmed closing time.
Right. I will ask at the next key handoff.
The caretaker was away when I stopped by, and the office note had no date.
Did Mara see who wrote it?
She did not. She only saw it beside the sign-in book.
The new schedule is still pending because the summer crew has not agreed on coverage.
Then the early-closing rumor remains unresolved.
Yes. Please keep the source attached if we mention it in the handoff.

expected.subject: Mara
expected.object: the north shed may close before dusk

evidence.quote: Mara thinks the north shed may close before dusk

messages.text: At Reef Station, we replaced the foam liner around the tide gauge housing.
Was the sensor recalibrated at the same time?
No, the calibration visit was moved to the following week.
The gauge read high the morning after the liner swap.
That timing might look connected.
The readings also rose at the neighboring inlet, so the liner change alone does not establish a cause.
The station log has the swap date and the first high reading.
Will you record them together?
I will list the dates separately until the technician compares both sensors.
The technician found salt on one connector, but has not tested the second gauge yet.
That does not settle whether the liner affected this reading.
Correct. We should keep the cause open until the comparison is finished.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: record the foam liner swap and next-morning high reading as separate dates until a technician compares both sensors

evidence.quote: we replaced the foam liner around the tide gauge housing
The gauge read high the morning after the liner swap.
I will list the dates separately until the technician compares both sensors

messages.text: The Bellweather lantern festival needs cue notes for the outdoor sound team.
Do you want one note per performer?
Last year I asked for notes grouped by performer, but that made the stage calls hard to scan.
I prefer cue cards ordered by show time now; the crew reads them at the stage edge.
Should the digital copy use the same order?
Yes, keep both versions in show-time order so a late cue is easy to spot.
The printer can make waterproof cards, though the ink test is not finished.
Will you switch to those?
I could consider them if the test survives the mist machine. I have not decided.
The ink smudged during the second mist test.
Then the waterproof cards are still an option, not a choice.
Exactly. We will use the ordinary stock for this rehearsal and review later.

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: cue cards ordered by show time

evidence.quote: I prefer cue cards ordered by show time now

expected.subject: the user
expected.object: could consider waterproof cue cards if the ink test survives the mist machine

evidence.quote: The printer can make waterproof cards, though the ink test is not finished.
I could consider them if the test survives the mist machine.

messages.text: The Windglass club has two glider cases, one slate and one red, and neither label lists the model.
Are you trying to identify which case fits the short-wing glider?
Maybe. Could you tell from the old packing photo, or is that one the spare sail bag?
If the short-wing frame fits the red case, we might borrow it for the hill launch.
Do you know the inside dimensions?
No, the ruler in the photo could be the six-inch one or the twelve-inch one.
The club list has two entries called "Juniper" and no owner initials.
Is Juniper a glider name or a case label?
That is what I am trying to work out. I do not want to reserve the wrong one.
Could the red case be borrowed if the other team has not packed it?
We would need to ask them and verify the dimensions first.
Yes, I am only sketching options for now; the launch date may move if the ridge is wet.
Mosslight Museum is testing two audio-guide layouts, a numbered route and a room-by-room route.
Which one did the visitors try yesterday?
I am not sure whether "the second one" means the route in the folder or the second recording.
If we moved the harbor recording earlier, would that make the stairs less crowded?
It might, but we would need visitor-flow notes.
The notes mention a queue near the blue door, but not which recording was playing.
Could the paper map be easier for the school group than the audio guide?
Possibly. Did the teacher ask for a different format?
She asked whether either option could work. I have not received a preference from her.
The editor asked if "that version" should go in the trial packet.
Can you tell which version the note refers to?
No, it only says version two. We should ask before changing the packet.
